messages:
alex: Hey — customer Brightframe reported vectors/sec dropped ~4x while tokens/sec stayed flat. Raising an escalation, share initial telemetry?
maria: ACK. Which customer plan + model?
alex: Brightframe prod, model=redwood-embed-lite-v2, dedicated pool us-west2, started ~08:10 UTC with alerts at 08:12. tokens/s ~1200 (normal), vectors/s ~300 (was ~1200).
tyler: I see a spike in gpu_queue_length and worker_wait_ms around the same time. Pasting short metrics: `gpu_queue_len=192 -> 800`, `worker_wait_ms p95 12ms -> 240ms`, `batch_window_ms avg 6 -> 18`
dina: Any auth/billing 429s or backend retries? Those can cause uneven batching and drop vectors throughput.
alex: No 429s in customer logs. There are intermittent 500s from vectorizer sidecar for a minute starting 08:11:22.
maria: sidecar 500s would block prod preprocess -> smaller batches or dropped requests? Can you grab sidecar logs and the kube events around that minute?
tyler: grabbing logs now. `kubectl -n redwood logs sidecar-bf-0 --since=5m` shows `ERROR: OOM while encoding tensor` then `restarted` 3 times.
dina: OOM in sidecar preproc explains tokens steady (text accepted) but vectors backlog since sidecar restarts. That would cause requests to pile up in the GPU queue — matches queue_len spike.
alex: Repro plan: run a small load test that simulates Brightframe payloads (avg doc len ~220 tokens, batch target 8) and artificially induce sidecar memory cap to reproduce. I'll share curl/harness.
maria: Also check if model variant rolled out earlier — variant with slower embedding kernel or different dim? If dim changed that could trigger conversion fallback and extra CPU work.
tyler: Model catalog shows no active rollout for that pool. But agent logs show a fallback to `redwood-embed-lite-v2-quant` for ~35s at 08:11:50 due to replica mismatch.
dina: Fallback to quant variant could change per-vector compute and queueing. Combined with sidecar OOM restarts this explains large vectors/sec drop while tokens/sec (ingest) looks fine.
alex: Repro command (local):
```bash
# simulate payload shape + small concurrency
python tools/loadgen.py --url https://api.redwood.net/v1/embeddings \
  --key $TEST_KEY --batch-size 8 --qps 50 --payload-file samples/brightframe.json
# then kill sidecar to mimic OOM restart
kubectl -n redwood exec -it sidecar-bf-0 -- bash -c 'kill -9 $(pidof sidecar)'
```
maria: Good. For short-term mitigation: increase sidecar memory request on that pool and pin model variant to non-quant in routing policy for Brightframe. Can infra patch autoscaler to prefer older variant?
tyler: I'll open a quick infra CL to bump sidecar mem from 512Mi -> 1Gi on the affected pool, and a routing policy pin.
dina: For postmortem, collect: sidecar logs, kube events, model-routing events, and per-request trace ids. Also capture kernel-level GPU metrics (`nvhost_queue_len`, `cuda_stalls`) for 08:05-08:20 window.
alex: I'll notify customer with status: suspected root cause = sidecar OOM causing restarts + brief fallback to quant variant => increased CPU preproc and GPU queue backlog => vectors/sec drop. ETA for mitigation: 30m.
maria: Thx. Adding SRE runbook note about monitoring sidecar restarts as fallback signal for embedding regressions :eyes: :thumbsup:
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-14732, assigned to eng-ml + eng-sre. Watchers: maria, tyler, alex, dina.
alex: Will follow up with repro artifacts and logs once upload finishes.
